findings.title: Split sub-requests are interpolated again by the backend path; sharded requests are interpolated three times
findings.body:
`runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` on every target. Each sub-request then goes through `datasource.runQuery`, which calls `super.query`, which calls `this.applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target again (`packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185`). The same happens in the unsplit path, but there it runs only once.

On the sharded path the pass runs three times. `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates once (`shardQuerySplitting.ts:52`). Every shard cycle then calls `runSplitQuery` (`shardQuerySplitting.ts:163`), which interpolates again, and the backend path interpolates a third time. This is why the updated test expects 5 calls instead of 1.

The passes are not free:
- `addAdHocFilters` (`datasource.ts:1073-1091`) calls `addLabelToQuery`, which does no de-duplication (`modifyQuery.ts:147`). With ad hoc filters set, the same matcher or `| key="v"` label filter is appended on each pass. For parsed labels the expression grows with every pass.
- Each pass re-runs `templateSrv.replace` on text that is already interpolated. Escaped values that contain `$name`, such as `\$name` from the regex-escape helper, can be substituted a second time.
- Each pass re-parses the query with lezer, once per target per shard cycle.

The fix is to interpolate once. Either interpolate in `runSplitQuery` only, and have `runShardSplitQuery` skip it because its sub-requests go through `runSplitQuery`. Or pass an option so `runSplitQuery` skips interpolation when the caller already did it. Then confirm whether `DataSourceWithBackend.query` can avoid re-interpolating.

findings.title: Test pins the redundant interpolation count instead of the behavior
findings.body: `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` encodes one call from `runShardSplitQuery` plus one per sub-request from `runSplitQuery`. The test name, 'Interpolates queries before running', says nothing about this. If the repeated interpolation is removed, this assertion breaks for no behavioral reason. If it stays, the number is hard to understand. Assert that the final `runQuery` targets are interpolated, as the sibling assertions already do, and drop or comment the count.

findings.title: New interpolation tests rely on a fake `replace` that does not match production behavior for `$__auto`
findings.body:
The tests mock `templateSrv.replace` to turn `$__auto` into `5m`. The real `applyTemplateVariables` removes `__auto`, `__interval`, `__range` and the related variables from `scopedVars` before replacing (`datasource.ts:1113`). Those variables are deliberately left for backend interpolation. The `[5m]` assertion therefore shows only that the mock was called. It does not show that `$__auto` is resolved in the splitting path.

The test also never checks that `step: '$step'` becomes the 5m step used by `calculateStep`, which is the point of interpolating before splitting. Use a variable name that the real implementation interpolates, such as a user variable. Add an assertion on the step-based grouping, for example on the partition size of the metric request. The same applies to `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:84-101`.

contracts.action: runSplitQuery now interpolates template variables and ad hoc filters on each target before partitioning
contracts.equivalent_path: DataSourceWithBackend.query interpolates via applyTemplateVariables on every target when runQuery runs (packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185); the non-split path in LokiDatasource.query relies on that single pass.
contracts.before_after: Before: splitting used raw expr/step, so calculateStep (querySplitting.ts:361-372) could not parse `$step`, and the grouping and partition decisions used uninterpolated expressions. After: the interpolated queries drive grouping and step partitioning. Each sub-request is then interpolated a second time by the backend path.
contracts.visible_effect: Step-based and `$__range` detection (isQueryWithRangeVariable) is evaluated on the interpolated expr. Chart step and splitting match user-variable values. Ad hoc filters can be appended more than once to the backend-bound expr.
contracts.failure_mode: A double-applied ad hoc filter makes the query longer but not semantically different. A value that contains a variable-like pattern could be substituted twice. There is no error or log. Reported as a finding.

contracts.equivalent_path: LokiDatasource.interpolateVariablesInQueries (datasource.ts:429-447) previously used here. applyTemplateVariables (datasource.ts:1110) is used by the backend path and by runLiveQueryThroughBackend (datasource.ts:377).
contracts.before_after: Before: variables were replaced using the full scopedVars, including `__interval`, and ad hoc filters were not passed in. The datasource ref was set. After: `__interval`, `__interval_ms`, `__range*` and `__auto` are left for the backend, `step` and `legendFormat` are interpolated, and ad hoc filters are applied. The datasource ref is no longer set here. The backend path sets it.
contracts.visible_effect: Sharded queries now respect ad hoc filters and step/legend interpolation, consistent with the non-sharded path. Sub-requests go through runSplitQuery and runQuery, so interpolation runs again.
contracts.failure_mode: Same repeated-interpolation cost as the other entry. No new failure path for fetchLabelValues, which is unchanged.

summary: The change makes `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery` interpolate variables, step and ad hoc filters up front through `applyTemplateVariables`. That is the right call, because step-based splitting now sees interpolated values. The cost is repeated interpolation: sub-requests are interpolated again in `DataSourceWithBackend.query`, and sharded requests go through three passes. The updated test's count of 5 calls shows this. I found no other defects. Two test comments: the fake `replace` mock in the new tests does not mirror how the real `applyTemplateVariables` leaves `$__auto` for the backend, and the call-count assertion pins the redundancy.
